questions.question: The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of a table is 3 ∶ 4. The shopkeeper gives two equal successive discounts of 25% on the marked price and sells the table for Rs. 2,250. Find the loss during this transaction.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP) ratio = 3 : 4

Final Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 2,250

Two successive discounts of 25% each

**Formula:**

Successive discounts calculation

Loss = CP - SP

**Solution:**

⇒ If MP is 4, then CP = 3 (from the ratio).

If SP after two discounts is 2,250,

then MP = 2,250 / [(1-25/100)²] = Rs. 4000.

⇒ CP = (3/4) × 4000 = Rs. 3000.

⇒ Loss = CP - SP = 3000 - 2250 = Rs. 750

**Therefore, the shopkeeper incurs a loss of Rs. 750 in this transaction.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper sells potatoes at Rs. 28/kg, which he bought at Rs. 25/kg, and he is giving 800 gm instead of 1000 gm. Find his actual profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of per kg potato is Rs. 28, cost price of per kg potato is Rs. 25 and he gave 800 gm. in place of 1000 gm.

**Formula used:**

Profit = selling price - cost price

Profit%(x) = dfrac{profit}{cost price} × 100

Profit%(y) = dfrac{error}{true weight - error} × 100

Error = true weight - false weight

Overall profit% = x + y + dfrac{xy}{100} [where, x and y are the profit%]

**Calculations:**

Profit in price of potato = Rs. (28 - 25) = Rs. 3

Profit%(x) = dfrac{3}{25} × 100 = 12%

This is the original profit If the shopkeeper has actually sold 1 kg of potato but here he used the false weight.

Error in weight = 1000 - 800 = 200 gm.

Profit %(y) = dfrac{200}{1000 - 200} × 100

= dfrac{200}{800} × 100 = 25%.

Overall profit% = 12 + 25 + dfrac{12 × 25}{100}

= 37 + 3 = 40%

**∴ The answer is 40%.**

Slant height l² = h² + (R − r)²

Volume V = (1/3)πh(R² + r² + Rr)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17586ab16c4c28e21927360e31d401ab86dd5db975054527063a9658aa9849ba.png]

Total Surface Area of Frustum

The total surface area includes the curved area and the area of both circular bases: TSA = πl(R + r) + πR² + πr².

questions.solution:
**Given:**

External radius (Rₑₓₜ) = 10.5 cm

Internal radius (Rᵢₙₜ) = 7.7 cm

Density of the metal (ρ) = 10.3 g/cm³

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4)/(3) pi r³ 

Volume of the hollow sphere = Volume of external sphere - Volume of internal sphere

Mass = Density × Volume

**Calculation:**

Volume of external sphere (Vₑₓₜ)

⇒ Vₑₓₜ = (4)/(3) pi (10.5)³

⇒ Vₑₓₜ = (4)/(3) times (22)/(7) times 1157.625 

⇒ Vₑₓₜ = 4852.5 cm³

Volume of internal sphere (Vᵢₙₜ)

⇒ Vᵢₙₜ = (4)/(3) pi (7.7)³

⇒ Vᵢₙₜ = (4)/(3) times (22)/(7) times 456.533 

⇒ Vᵢₙₜ = 1980 cm³

Volume of the hollow sphere (V)

⇒ V = Vₑₓₜ - Vᵢₙₜ

⇒ V = 4852.5 - 1980

⇒ V = 2872.5 cm³

Mass (m)

⇒ m = ρ × V

⇒ m = 10.3 × 2872.5

⇒ m = 29587.75 g

Convert g to kg

⇒ m = 29587.75 / 1000

⇒ m ≈ 29.6 kg

Rounded off to the nearest tens, mass = 30 kg

**The mass of the sphere is 30 kg.**

• Under the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Samhita (BNSS)**, the provision for **default bail** is applicable in cases where the investigation is not completed within the prescribed timeline.
 
• For **minor offences**, the timeline for completing investigations is **60 days**. If the investigation is not completed within this period, the accused becomes eligible for default bail.
 
• This provision ensures that individuals accused of minor offences are not subjected to prolonged incarceration without trial. *Hence, the correct timeline is 60 days.*

• The provision for default bail under the BNSS is rooted in the principle of safeguarding individual liberty. It ensures that no one is detained indefinitely without proper legal justification.
 
• The timeline for investigations under the BNSS is strictly enforced to encourage efficiency and accountability in the police force.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about molecules of elements is correct?

options.text: Molecular oxygen and ozone are both molecules of the same element.
Diatomic molecules only contain atoms of different elements.
All elements exist as monoatomic molecules in nature.
A molecule of phosphorus always contains five atoms.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is:** "Molecular oxygen and ozone are both molecules of the same element."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Elemental Molecules:**

 
 
• An elemental molecule is made up of atoms of the same chemical element bonded together.
 
• For example, oxygen exists in nature as O₂ (molecular oxygen) and O₃ (ozone), both containing only oxygen atoms.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Oxygen (O₂): **
 
 
• It is a diatomic molecule comprising two oxygen atoms bonded together.
 
• Molecular oxygen is essential for respiration in most living organisms.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃): **
 
 
• It is a triatomic molecule made up of three oxygen atoms bonded together.
 
• Ozone plays a crucial role in absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation in the Earth's stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Commonality:**
 
 
• Both O₂ and O₃ are allotropes of the element oxygen, differing in molecular composition but made of the same element.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Diatomic molecules only contain atoms of different elements."**

 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** Diatomic molecules can be either homonuclear (same element, e.g., O₂, N₂, H₂) or heteronuclear (different elements, e.g., HCl, CO).
 
• **Correct Concept:** Diatomic refers to the number of atoms, not the type of atoms involved.
 
 
 
• **"All elements exist as monoatomic molecules in nature."**
 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** While noble gases like helium (He), neon (Ne), and argon (Ar) exist as monoatomic gases, many other elements exist as diatomic or polyatomic molecules (e.g., O₂, N₂, S₈).
 
• **Correct Concept:** The physical form of an element depends on its chemical bonding and stability in nature.
 
 
 
• **"A molecule of phosphorus always contains five atoms."**
 
 
• **Incorrect Explanation:** Phosphorus typically exists as P₄ molecules, meaning it contains four phosphorus atoms in a tetrahedral arrangement.
 
• **Correct Concept:** There is no common form of phosphorus containing five atoms in a single molecule.
